title: Put four code-shape rules in the worker brief
action:
Per D1-D5 in docs/history/code-shape-doctrine/CONTEXT.md. Add ONE short block to the `Contract:` list in packages/bee/prompts/worker-cell.md (the SOURCE — D4; never .bee/bin/prompts/worker-cell.md, which bee onboard --apply regenerates and would silently discard).

The four rules, and nothing beyond them (D2):
- Prefer deletion before addition.
- The smallest diff that solves it.
- A signal threaded through several layers means stop and find the direct path.
- Leave the base simpler than you found it.

Write them as a worker reads them at the moment it writes code — imperative, concrete, no theory. Keep the block SHORT: this prompt is inlined into every dispatched worker's first message, so every line is paid for on every cell in every host repo. Match the surrounding contract bullets' voice.

D3: nothing refuses. Say so in the block itself, in the same posture as the existing red-before-green rule at skills/bee-swarming/references/worker-details.md:33-35 — 'craft, applied by judgment and enforced by review, not by flags'. Do NOT edit worker-details.md; cite it if a pointer helps, the way the class playbooks already point at it.

Then read packages/bee/agents/bee-build.md.tmpl:9, which carries its own `Contract:` block, and answer the CONTEXT.md execution question: if that block already duplicates the brief's contract bullets, add the same block there; if it points at the brief instead, add a pointer. Match what the file already does — do not invent a new split. Say in the cap which it was and why.

Run the full `bee dev regen` chain (render-skill-trees, then onboard --repo-root . --apply, then release-manifest --write, in that order) so the installed copy under .bee/bin/prompts/ picks the change up, and verify both copies carry it.
verify: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --no-fail-fast --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml && .bee/bin/bee onboard --repo-root . --json && .bee/bin/bee dev release-manifest --check
acceptance: packages/bee/prompts/worker-cell.md carries the four rules in its Contract block, stating they are judgment-and-review, never a refusal. .bee/bin/prompts/worker-cell.md carries the same text after onboard --apply. bee-build.md.tmpl was read and handled to match its existing pattern, with the choice named in the cap. worker-details.md is unedited. The suite is green and onboard reports up_to_date.

truths: the four rules appear in packages/bee/prompts/worker-cell.md's Contract block, and nowhere does the block add a fifth rule or a types/domain-modelling rule
the block states plainly that nothing refuses — it is judgment, surfaced at review
the SOURCE was edited, and .bee/bin/prompts/worker-cell.md carries the same text only because onboard --apply installed it
bee-build.md.tmpl was read and the cap names whether it got the block or a pointer, and why that matches what the file already does
cargo test is green and bee onboard --repo-root . --json reports up_to_date
